abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.p: Trophoblast stem cells, derived from the trophectoderm of the blastocyst, are used as an in vitro model to reveal the mechanisms underlying placentation in mammals. In humans, suitable culture conditions for trophoblast stem cell derivation have recently been established. The established human trophoblast stem cells differentiate efficiently toward two trophoblast subtypes: syncytiotrophoblasts and extravillous trophoblasts. However, the efficiency of differentiation is lower in macaque trophoblast stem cells than in human trophoblast stem cells. Here, we demonstrate that the activation of Wnt signaling downregulated the expression of inhibitory G protein and induced trophoblastic lineage switching to the syncytiotrophoblast progenitor state. The treatment of macaque trophoblast stem cells with a GSK-3 inhibitor, CHIR99021, upregulated syncytiotrophoblast progenitor markers and enhanced proliferation. Under the Wnt signaling–activated conditions, macaque trophoblast stem cells effectively differentiated to syncytiotrophoblasts upon dibutyryl cyclic AMP (dbcAMP) and forskolin treatment. RNA-seq analyses revealed the downregulation of inhibitory G protein, which may make macaque trophoblast stem cells responsive to forskolin. Interestingly, this lineage switching appeared to be reversible as the macaque trophoblast stem cells lost responsiveness to forskolin upon the removal of CHIR99021. The ability to regulate the direction of macaque trophoblast stem cell differentiation would be advantageous in elucidating the mechanisms underlying placentation in non-human primates.
The activation of Wnt signaling in macaque trophoblast stem cell lines potentiated differentiation toward syncytiotrophoblast cell fate.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: The placenta functions as a maternal–fetal junction in mammals to supply nutrition to the fetus, exchange gases, and remove waste from the fetus during pregnancy. In human and non-human primate placenta, there are three major trophoblast subtypes: proliferative cytotrophoblasts (CTBs), multinucleated syncytiotrophoblasts (STBs), and invasive extravillous trophoblasts (EVTs). Cytotrophoblasts are classified by their location and differentiation ability into two groups, villous cytotrophoblasts (vCTBs) and cell column trophoblasts (CCTs), which differentiate into STBs and EVTs, respectively [1–3]. Trophoblast stem cells (TSCs), capable of differentiating toward all trophoblast subtypes in the placenta, were first isolated from mouse blastocysts [4]. The derivation of mouse TSCs accelerated elucidation of the mechanisms behind placental formation, trophoblast differentiation, and transcription factor networks critical for maintaining TSCs’ stemness [5–8]. Although the culture conditions for mouse TSCs failed to establish human TSCs (hTSCs) from the blastocysts [9], human and macaque TSC lines were recently obtained from blastocyst and/or placenta under culture conditions differing from those of mouse TSCs [10–12]. These TSCs should provide powerful tools to understand human and non-human primate placental formation and reveal the molecular mechanisms underlying pregnancy-associated diseases caused by placental disorders.

The Wnt signaling pathway, evolutionarily conserved from hydra to humans, plays important roles in embryonic development, cell proliferation, and differentiation [13, 14]. A GSK3β inhibitor, CHIR99021, activates the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway by inhibiting the degradation of β-catenin [14–16]. CHIR99021 promotes trophoblast cell differentiation toward syncytiotrophoblast layer II cells in mice, whereas it is essential for maintaining TSCs and primary cytotrophoblasts in humans [10, 17, 18]. Thus, the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway is profoundly associated with trophoblastic features, but its physiological function appears to differ among mammalian species. We recently established TSC lines from cynomolgus monkey blastocysts (macTSCs) [11]. The macTSCs were established and maintained without CHIR99021 or other Wnt/β-catenin signaling activators, suggesting that the activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway is dispensable for at least the maintenance of TSCs in the cynomolgus monkey. To explore a function of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in trophoblast cells in cynomolgus monkey, we here investigated the effects of CHIR99021 on macTSCs.

sec.title: macTSC culture
sec.p: macTSCs were cultured in TS medium consisting of RPMI-1640 (189-02025; Wako, Osaka, Japan) supplemented with 20% fetal bovine serum (S1810-500; Biowest, Nuaillé, France), 2 mM L-glutamine (073-05391; Wako), 1 mM sodium pyruvate (190-14881; Wako), 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol (133-14571; Wako), 25 ng/ml FGF4 (062-04341; Wako), 1 μg/ml heparin (H3149; Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA), 1 μM BMS493 (3509; TOCRIS, Bristol, UK), and 10 μM Y-27632 (034-24024; Wako) [CHIR(−) condition]. For the CHIR(+) condition, 3 μM CHIR99021 (034-23103; Wako) was added to the TS medium. The cells were incubated at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2, and the culture medium was replaced once every 2 days.

sec.title: Syncytiotrophoblast differentiation
sec.p: For STB differentiation, macTSCs were cultured for 6 days in the TS medium with 1 mM dbcAMP (D0260; Sigma-Aldrich) or 2 μM forskolin (FSK; 063-02191; Wako), but without FGF4, heparin, BMS493, and Y-27632. The culture medium was replaced once every 2 days.

sec.title: Growth curves
sec.p: Cells were seeded in six-well plates at 1.0 × 105 per well and precultured for 1 day in the CHIR(−) condition. Then, the cells were re-fed with fresh TS medium supplemented with or without CHIR99021. Cells were counted on days 0, 2, and 4 using a Countess automated cell counter (Invitrogen, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA).

sec.title: RNA extraction and quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR)
sec.p: Total RNAs were extracted using TRI Reagent (TR118; Molecular Research Center, Cincinnati, OH, USA), in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions. cDNA was synthesized using ReverTra Ace qPCR RT Master Mix with gDNA Remover (FSQ-301; TOYOBO, Osaka, Japan). qRT-PCR was performed using FastStart Essential DNA Green Master (06402712001; Roche, Basel, Switzerland). Amplification and fluorescence detection were carried out using a Light Cycler 96 (Roche). The primers used in this study are presented in Table S1.

sec.title: RNA-seq analyses
sec.p: Total RNAs from macTSC#2 and #4 cultured under CHIR(−) and CHIR(+) conditions were used for RNA-seq. Library preparation and sequencing were outsourced at Filgen. Prepared cDNA libraries were sequenced with NovaSeq (Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA). Upon the receipt of RNA-seq data, reads were mapped on the cynomolgus monkey genome (macFas 5.0) using HISAT2 with a transcript assembly to guide mapping. Putative transcripts were identified in macTSCs using Stringtie. Reads from all samples were counted and assigned to genes in the assembled genome model using FeatureCounts, and the count table was loaded into DESeq2 to detect differentially expressed genes. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) was performed using GSEA v4.0.3 Mac App from Broad Institute (software.broadinstitute.org/gsea/index.jsp). Hallmark gene sets (h.all.v7.0.symbols.gmt) and gene ontology (GO) gene sets (c5.all.v7.0.symbols.gmt) were used. Other analyses, including statistical analyses, were performed using R packages (https://www.r-project.org/). The raw and processed data are available at the GEO database (GSE241665).

sec.title: Immunocytochemistry
sec.p: Cells grown on coverslips were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS(−). The fixed cells were permeabilized with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS(−) and incubated with 5% BSA and 0.1% Tween-20 in PBS(−) overnight. Subsequently, the cells were incubated with primary antibodies at 4°C overnight. The signals were visualized by secondary antibodies. The primary and secondary antibodies used in this study are listed in Table S2. After nuclear counterstaining with DAPI (D523; DOJINDO, Kumamoto, Japan), the cells were mounted on glass slides with VECTASHIELD (H-1000; Vector Laboratories, Newark, CA, USA). In this study, we defined the cells containing three or more nuclei as multinucleated STBs. The intensity of nuclear staining was measured using CellProfiler (https://cellprofiler.org/). The ratio of STBs was calculated as the percentage fluorescence intensity of nuclei contained in STBs relative to the fluorescence intensity of all nuclei in each of four randomly chosen fields of biological duplicates.

sec.title: Protein extraction and zymography
sec.p: Total protein was extracted with the radioimmunoprecipitation assay (RIPA) buffer (SC-24948; Santa Cruz Biotechnology, Dallas, TX, USA) containing 1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF) (37495; ACTIVE MOTIF, Carlsbad, CA, USA). Total proteins (5 μg) were then separated by sodium dodecyl sulfatepolyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) using 10% acrylamide gel containing 1.0 mg/ml gelatin. After the electrophoresis, the gel was incubated twice in renaturation solution (2.5% Triton X-100) for 40 min each, followed by overnight incubation in developing buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.4, 200 mM NaCl, 5 mM CaCl2, and 1% Triton X-100) at 37°C. After incubation, the gel was stained with Coomassie blue stain and de-stained using 30% methanol/10% acetic acid solution until the bands became visible.

sec.title: Statistical analyses
sec.p: All statistical analyses were performed using R, and a p-value or padj < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Two-tailed Student t-tests were performed for the data in Figure 1C and D. The Tukey–Kramer test was performed for the data in Figures 1B, 2C, D, F, and G, 3C and E, 4C and E, S2B and D, and S3. The padj values were calculated using DESeq2.

sec.title: Wnt/β-catenin signaling activation promotes villous cytotrophoblast marker expression and proliferation of macTSCs
sec.p: First, we cultured macTSCs (macTSC#2 line) in the presence of CHIR99021 [CHIR(+)]. Compared with the colonies in the control [CHIR(−)], which appeared thin and flat, macTSCs formed thicker colonies with bright edges under a phase-contrast microscope in the CHIR(+) condition (Figures 1A and S1). The expression level of TEAD4, a vCTB marker [19], was also shown to be upregulated by the addition of CHIR99021 in a dose-dependent manner, with 3–10 μM CHIR99021 showing the highest TEAD4 expression (Figure 1B). From these results, we decided to use 3 μM CHIR99021 for further experiments.

After the induction of differentiation, the proliferation of mouse TSCs slows down and they eventually stop dividing [4, 20]. Hence, the maintenance of proliferative capacity is convenient as an indicator of an undifferentiated state. The CHIR(+) condition significantly enhanced the proliferation of macTSCs to approximately twice the speed of that in the control (Figure 1C). Because these results suggested that Wnt signaling in macTSCs helps them to maintain an undifferentiated state, we also analyzed the expression of vCTB markers by qRT-PCR, finding that not only TEAD4 but also other vCTB marker genes—EPCAM, TP63, and VGLL1 [19, 21, 22]—were significantly upregulated in the CHIR(+) condition (Figure 1D).

sec.title: Pre-activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling enhances efficiency of syncytiotrophoblast differentiation
sec.p: Second, we investigated the effect of CHIR99021 on the differentiation capacity of macTSCs. After 3 days of culture with or without 3 μM CHIR99021, we cultured macTSCs in the differentiation medium (the macTSC medium with cyclic AMP (cAMP)) [11] for another 6 days (Figure 2A). While TEAD4 was upregulated in the CHIR(+) condition at day 3, its expression was downregulated in both differentiation conditions at day 9 (Figure 2B), suggesting that cAMP treatment induced the differentiation of macTSCs regardless of the pre-activation of Wnt signaling. Preculturing in the CHIR(+) condition induced the formation of larger multinucleated STBs after cAMP treatment [CHIR(+) cAMP] than for the cells precultured without CHIR99021 [CHIR(−) cAMP] (Figure 2C). The expression of STB markers—GCM1, ERVV-1, ERVV-2, CGA, and CGB [23–25]—was significantly increased in CHIR(+) cAMP compared with that in the CHIR(−) cAMP condition (Figure 2D). In addition, large multinucleated STBs, lacking E-cadherin expression, were observed in the CHIR(+) cAMP condition (Figure 2E). These STBs strongly expressed chorionic gonadotropin (CG), which is one of the pregnancy hormones secreted by STBs in vivo. Moreover, the ratio of multinucleated cells was increased in CHIR(+) cAMP (Figure 2F). These results show that activating Wnt signaling in undifferentiated macTSCs enhances their potential to differentiate toward STBs. Meanwhile, the expression level of ITGA5, one of the EVT markers [26], in CHIR(+) cAMP was not significantly different from that in the control, while another EVT marker, CDH5 [27], showed the highest expression in CHIR(+) cAMP (Figure 2G). Human EVTs that invade maternal decidua express MMP2 and MMP9 [28]. MMP2 mRNA expression in CHIR(+) cAMP was lower than in the CHIR(−) cAMP condition. Gelatin zymography revealed that the enzymatic activities of both MMP2 and MMP9 were suppressed in CHIR(+) cAMP (Figure 2H). Thus, Wnt signaling activation in the undifferentiated macTSCs enhances the capacity of macTSCs to differentiate toward STBs at the expense of EVTs.

sec.title: Wnt/β-catenin signaling activation confers forskolin responsiveness on macTSCs
sec.p: dbcAMP permeates through the cytoplasmic membrane and acts as a second messenger to activate downstream target genes of cAMP signaling in human placental cells [29]. In contrast, FSK indirectly increases the intracellular concentration of cAMP by maintaining the active form of adenylate cyclase on the plasma membrane [30] and induces STB differentiation of human trophoblast cells [10, 31]. Whereas FSK is widely used for STB differentiation in human trophoblasts, FSK did not induce STB differentiation of macTSCs in our preliminary experiments. Given the improved STB differentiation in the CHIR(+) condition, we hypothesized that FSK might also be effective. We then investigated whether FSK induces STB differentiation of CHIR99021-treated macTSCs by culturing macTSCs in TS medium without FGF4, heparin, BMS493, and Y-27632, supplemented with 0 or 2 μM FSK for 6 days following 3 days of preculture under the CHIR(−) or CHIR(+) condition [CHIR(−) FSK and CHIR(+) FSK, respectively; Figure 3A]. In accordance with the preliminary results, the formation of multinucleated cells was not observed, and the STB markers were not upregulated in the CHIR(−) FSK condition (Figure 3B and C). In contrast, we identified the formation of multinucleated STBs in the CHIR(+) FSK condition (Figure 3B). The expression of STB markers—GCM1, ERVV-1, ERVV-2, CGA, and CGB—was also significantly increased in the CHIR(+) FSK condition (Figure 3C). Immunocytochemistry revealed large multinucleated STBs, as seen in the CHIR(+) cAMP condition (Figures 2E and 3D). Moreover, the ratio of STBs in the CHIR(+) FSK condition (48.5 ± 19.7%) was higher than in the CHIR(+) cAMP condition (29.3 ± 11.4%), showing the augmentation of STB differentiation efficiency (Figures 2F and 3E). These results suggest that Wnt signaling activation conferred FSK responsiveness on macTSCs.

sec.title: Wnt/β-catenin signaling reversibly controls trophoblastic cell fate
sec.p: CHIR99021 promotes trophoblast cell differentiation in mice [17]; however, our current results showed that Wnt signaling activation in macTSCs enhances cell proliferation and upregulates vCTB markers (Figure 1). Differentiation analyses also revealed that macTSCs gained high efficiency in differentiating toward STBs upon CHIR99021 treatment (Figures 2 and 3).

Next, we investigated whether modulation of the direction of differentiation of macTSCs by activating Wnt signaling is reversible. To address this, we put macTSCs back in the CHIR(−) condition after preculturing in the CHIR(+) condition for 3 days (Figure 4A). Notably, tight macTSC colonies that appeared under the CHIR(+) condition returned to exhibiting a flatter and thinner morphology under the CHIR(−) condition [“C(+/−)” in Figure 4B]. The expression of vCTB markers, TEAD4 and VGLL1, decreased following the change of culture condition from CHIR(+) to CHIR(−) (Figure 4C). Meanwhile, another vCTB marker, TP63, maintained a higher expression level even after returning to the CHIR(−) condition. These results showed that the effects of CHIR on macTSCs’ morphology and gene expression are reversible. It was also suggested that the degree of decline in gene expression levels upregulated by CHIR99021 varies depending on the gene. When we induced STB differentiation by FSK treatment after the different combinations of CHIR99021 preculture (Figure 4D), the expression of STB marker genes was significantly upregulated only when we cultured cells in the CHIR(+) condition immediately before the induction of differentiation (Figure 4E). To verify that the abovementioned effects of CHIR99021 are not unique to the macTSC#2 line, we also analyzed the effects on the FSK responsiveness of another line, macTSC#4, which formed a unique branch in the hierarchical clustering analysis of transcriptomes among all five macTSC lines (11). As a result, we obtained similar results (Figure S2A and B). The expression levels of STB markers in macTSC#4 also depended on the preculture conditions immediately before FSK treatment (Figure S2C and D). Thus, macTSCs transiently gained FSK responsiveness by Wnt signaling activation.

sec.title: Wnt/β-catenin signaling may contribute to intracellular cAMP production via the downregulation of Gi-associated gene expression
sec.p: To understand how CHIR99021 confers FSK responsiveness on macTSCs, we analyzed the expression levels of the adenylate cyclase family by qRT-PCR. However, the results showed no difference in the expression of ADCY3, ADCY5, ADCY6, ADCY7, and ADCY9, regardless of Wnt signaling activation (Figure S3).

For further analysis to reveal the regulators of FSK responsiveness in macTSCs, we performed RNA-seq analysis on macTSCs cultured with or without CHIR99021. Compared with the findings under the CHIR(−) condition, 121 upregulated and 300 downregulated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were detected in the CHIR(+) condition (Figure 5A and Table 1). Principal component analysis (PCA) with all genes and hierarchical clustering analysis with DEGs showed that the difference in gene expression profile was greater between culture conditions than between cell lines (Figure 5B and C). PPARD and TCF7, downstream of Wnt/β-catenin signaling [32], were upregulated by CHIR99021 treatment (Figure 5C), indicating that the Wnt signaling pathway is activated in macTSCs by CHIR99021 treatment. Remarkably, we found a significant increase in the expression level of OVOL1, which is highly expressed in vCTBs [33], under the CHIR(+) condition. Syncytiotrophoblasts are formed via cell fusion caused by the expression of endogenous retrovirus envelope genes [24, 34]. Interestingly, GSEA revealed that the CHIR(+) condition was enriched for genes related to “viral gene expression” (Figure 5D). Given these results, we hypothesize that Wnt signaling activation led to a transition of macTSCs to a vCTB-like, STB progenitor state.

(A) An MAplot drawn using whole RNA-seq data of macTSC#2 and #4 cultured with/without CHIR99021. DEGs (121 upregulated, shown in red; 300 downregulated, shown in blue) were detected by DESeq2 (padj < 0.05, fold change ≥2). (B) PCA of macTSCs with/without CHIR99021. (C) Heatmap for 421 DEGs with Z-scores as expression values among all samples. Clustering analysis was performed using the Euclidean distance and the farthest neighbor method. (D) GSEA for “viral gene expression” performed using all gene expression data of RNA-seq (nominal p-value <0.05, FDR < 0.25). (F) The expression levels of Gi-associated genes with notable change. The expression value, transcripts per million, was calculated from RNA-seq read count data, and the mean values (±SD) of technical duplicates of biological duplicates are shown. *, padj < 0.05.

sec.p: Intracellular cAMP is generated from ATP via adenylate cyclase activity, regulated through the binding of stimulatory (Gs) and inhibitory (Gi) G proteins [35]. Because there were no differences in the expression levels of adenylate cyclase genes between CHIR(−) and CHIR(+) conditions (Figure S3), we focused on G proteins and G protein-associated genes. The RNA-seq data showed that some of the Gi-related genes were commonly downregulated in the CHIR(+) condition (Figure 5E). EDN1, DRD2, PTGER3, and GNAI1 in particular appeared to be significantly decreased in the CHIR(+) condition (Figure 5F). Thus, the acquisition of FSK responsiveness may involve the suppression of Gi-related genes upon CHIR99021 treatment.

sec.title: Wnt/β-catenin signal activation suppresses extravillous trophoblast lineage marker gene expression
sec.p: Extravillous trophoblasts, as another trophoblastic subtype, infiltrate uterine decidua and remodel the maternal spiral artery to increase blood flow into the intervillous space of the placenta [36, 37]. It was also reported that primary CTBs, isolated from the human placenta, easily differentiate into EVTs upon being placed in hypoxic culture conditions in vitro [38]. During EVT differentiation, trophoblasts develop invasive potential via epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) [39]. Among the 300 downregulated DEGs identified in the CHIR(+) condition (Figure 5B), GO terms related to the phenotype of EVTs, such as cell migration, extracellular matrix organization, blood vessel morphogenesis, and cellular response to hypoxia, were enriched among the top 20 (Figure S4A). Meanwhile, among the 300 downregulated DEGs, 42 genes were primarily associated with one or two of these five GO terms (Figure S4B). GSEA similarly confirmed the enrichment of genes related to EMT and hypoxia among the downregulated DEGs (Figure S4C and D). These results support our hypothesis that Wnt signaling activation converts macTSCs to vCTB-like cells rather than an EVT progenitor state.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: CHIR99021 is crucial in maintaining hTSCs in an undifferentiated state [10, 18]. In contrast, although CHIR99021 is dispensable for the maintenance of macTSCs [11], our current results showed that CHIR99021 treatment enhanced macTSCs’ proliferation and increased the levels of some of the vCTB markers (Figure 1). Wnt signaling activation by CHIR99021 not only altered the gene expression profile of macTSCs but also shifted the preference of their differentiation direction. Syncytiotrophoblast differentiation was not so efficient when cells were maintained under the previous culture condition (CHIR(−); designated as FHBY in our 2020 report [11]), whereas preculture in the CHIR(+) condition for a relatively short period (3 days) dramatically improved the STB formation rate, which led to higher expression of STB markers after the induction of differentiation (Figure 2). Moreover, although we could not induce STB differentiation using FSK under the CHIR(−) condition, the CHIR99021 treatment conferred FSK responsiveness on macTSCs, probably through the suppression of Gi-associated gene expression (Figures 3 and 5). Notably, the effect of CHIR99021 treatment on the cell differentiation potential was reversible and lost by 3 days of culture back in the CHIR(−) condition (Figure 4). These results suggest that CHIR99021 reversibly converts macTSCs to vCTB-like cells, which more easily differentiate toward multinucleated STBs (Figure 6).

caption.p: Activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling switches macTSCs to vCTB-like lineage. Under the CHIR(−) condition, macTSCs do not exhibit FSK responsiveness, and the induction of STB differentiation is not efficient. However, when macTSCs are culture with CHIR99021, a transition to a vCTB-like, STB progenitor state occurs. This transition is accompanied by an increased expression of vCTB marker genes, and importantly, the macTSCs acquire FSK responsiveness. This lineage switching is reversible as macTSCs lose FSK responsiveness after removing CHIR99021.

sec.p: The reversal of macTSCs' phenotype from a vCTB-like state to their original, EVT progenitor–like state was associated with a downregulation of the vCTB marker TEAD4 (Figure 4C). Interestingly, however, other vCTB markers, VGLL1 and TP63, behaved differently. Whereas VGLL1 tended to decrease but not significantly, TP63 remained higher for at least 3 days after the removal of CHIR99021. This may suggest that Wnt/ß-catenin signaling regulates the expression of these transcription factors differently. We speculate that TP63 is indirectly upregulated in response to the activation of Wnt/ß-catenin signaling so that the withdrawal of CHIR99021 does not immediately shut down the expression of TP63. These results also suggested that TP63 alone, or in combination with VGLL1, is insufficient to maintain a vCTB-like state, although TP63 inhibits EVT phenotype and maintains a cytotrophoblast stem cell–like state in human trophoblast [21].

Our RNA-seq data showed upregulation of the genes of the “viral gene expression” gene set in the CHIR(+) condition (Figure 5D). This gene set includes genes related to viral transcription, processing of viral transcripts, and viral translation, implying that CHIR(+) condition made the endogenous retrovirus genes prone to expression in macTSCs, which we hypothesize reflects a vCTB-like STB progenitor state. In support of this was the drastic upregulation of ERVV-1 and ERVV-2 by cAMP or FSK treatment when macTSCs were precultured in the CHIR(+) condition (Figures 2D and 3C). This STB progenitor state appeared to be transient since the withdrawal of CHIR99021 reversed macTSCs’ morphology, gene expression profile, and FSK responsiveness (Figure 4). Recently, the contribution of transposable elements to not only STB but also EVT differentiation as enhancers or promoters was reported in humans [40]. Further research is required to elucidate the molecular basis regulating endogenous retroviruses and transposable elements during placentation, which would allow us to modulate the differentiation potential of macTSCs.

Cell column trophoblasts, which are regarded as progenitors of invasive EVTs, have similar gene expression profiles to another type of progenitor cells, vCTBs, in humans [41–43]. CCTs are considered to be derived from vCTBs, with some slight changes in gene expression occurring during the migration into the maternal decidua. For example, the expression pattern of the adhesion molecules integrins gradually switches from proximal to distal of the placental villi [26]. Our RNA-seq analysis revealed that the expression of some of the CCT (CD9 and ITGA5) and EVT (ITGA5, ITGAV, FN1, PLAC8, and MMP9) markers [10, 26, 28, 44, 45] was higher in the CHIR(−) condition than in the CHIR99021-treated macTSCs (Figure S5 and Table 1), which suggests that macTSCs cultured under the CHIR(−) condition resemble the CCT/EVT cell lineage. CDH5 (VE-cadherin) protein expression has been demonstrated in the CCTs and decidua [27]. However, CDH5 mRNA was drastically increased in the CHIR(+) cAMP condition (Figure 2G). Recently, single-cell RNA-seq analyses indicated that the expression level of CDH5 mRNA is low in all trophoblast subtypes compared with that in the non-trophoblastic cell types in the human placenta [43], suggesting that CDH5 mRNA may not be an adequate marker for trophoblast cells, including CCTs and EVTs. To shed light on this complexity, we should establish conditions that promote the EVT differentiation of macTSCs. This will allow us to reveal gene/protein expression profiles of progenitors of and mature EVTs to focus on the signaling pathway(s) that is activated only in the CHIR(−) condition.

CHIR99021 conferred FSK responsiveness on macTSCs. Remarkably, EDN1, DRD2, PTGER3, and GNAI1 were detected as downregulated DEGs in our RNA-seq data for the CHIR(+) condition (Figure 5F). EDN1 acts as a ligand for Gi G-protein-coupled receptor in an autocrine and paracrine manner [46]. The downregulation of the ligands and receptors for Gi might have caused a decrease in GNAI1 expression. Meanwhile, the expression levels of adenylate cyclase gene family members, which produce intracellular cAMP, were not changed by the CHIR99021 treatment (Figure S3). These findings suggest that the activation of Wnt signaling in macTSCs contributes to suppressing Gi genes but not the regulation of adenylate cyclases. In addition, only 421 genes were detected as DEGs between the CHIR(−) and CHIR(+) conditions (Figure 5B and C). The change in expression of a limited number of Gi-associated ligands and receptors might enable the reversible change of differentiation potential of macTSCs.

The culture conditions of macTSCs conducted in this study differ from those of hTSCs, which may be reflected in macTSCs’ lower differentiation efficiency compared to hTSCs. Human TSCs are routinely maintained with CHIR99021, and switching to an FSK medium induces STB differentiation. In contrast to the simple STB induction, EVT induction requires preculture with two different types of media, with and without NRG1, for 3 days each without CHIR [10], hinting that hTSCs are skewed to the STB progenitor state. In support of this notion, the transcriptomic analyses by bulk- and single-nucleus RNA-seq revealed that hTSCs resemble vCTB (STB progenitor) of in vivo placentas [10, 47]. Although other cynomolgus monkey TSC lines have been established from placental villi under the culture conditions of hTSCs, their differentiation efficiency was also low and not as tightly controlled as hTSCs in a cell type–specific manner [12]. Even in the primates, there are anatomical differences in the placenta. For example, the macaque placentas have a unique structure between the placental villi and the decidua, the trophoblastic shell, which is not found in humans [48]. Differences in signaling pathways required for maintaining TSCs, and controlling their differentiation may also exist between monkeys and humans. Further examination is required to determine whether our findings of the effects of CHIR99021 are a consequence of different culture conditions or species differences.

In conclusion, we here demonstrated that activating Wnt signaling shifts differentiation potential toward STBs in macTSCs. The ability to regulate the direction of macTSC differentiation would be advantageous as an in vitro tool for elucidating the mechanisms underlying placentation and placental disorder using non-human primate models.
